parole.significato: -able; create an adjective from a noun or verb
parole.testo: From Old Swedish -bar, borrowed from Middle Low German -bar, from Old Saxon -bari. Cognate with native Old Swedish -bǣr (Old Norse -bærr), German -bar (from Old High German -bāri), Dutch -baar, Old English -bære.

From Old Swedish lykta, from Middle Low German luchte, ultimately derived from Old High German and Old Saxon lioht (“light”). Cognate with Danish lygte, Norwegian lykt.

From Middle Low German pracht, from Old High German braht (“crackling noise”), from Proto-Germanic *brahtaz (“cracking, snapping”), referring to the sound of applause. Influenced by German prangen (“to show off”).

parole.significato: square, tile, box (as on a checkerboard)
parole.testo: From Middle Low German rūte, from Old High German rūta, probably from Latin rūta (“rue”). Cognates include Danish rude, Norwegian Bokmål rute and German Raute (“rhomb”).
